strengths: Well-motivated probabilistic framework that principally addresses the important problem of composing heterogeneous models (generative, discriminative, physics-based) at inference time without retraining
Theoretically grounded use of Annealed Importance Sampling and Sequential Monte Carlo with clear formulations bridging theory to implementation
Training-free and modular approach enabling flexible composition of diverse expert types across multiple modalities
Demonstrates versatility across four distinct applications (image editing, physics-guided video, text-to-image, autoregressive models)
Includes ablation studies on conditional sampling showing concrete benefits, with detailed implementation descriptions for reproducibility
Shows improvements in controllability and alignment to input specifications compared to monolithic baselines, with comprehensive evaluation metrics
weaknesses: Prohibitive computational cost (4-30 minutes per sample using dual H200 GPUs) compared to feedforward inference, severely limiting practical applicability and real-world deployment

Severely limited baseline comparisons: only RF-Solver in Section 4.2, and monolithic variants in 4.3; critically, no comparisons with other compositional generation methods cited in related work (refs 10, 11, 12, 28, 31, 41)
Small-scale evaluation: 30 scenes in 4.2, 12 scenes in 4.3, limited qualitative examples in 4.4; no human evaluation studies to validate subjective quality or user preferences

Expert compatibility assumption inadequately addressed: paper acknowledges sampling requires 'reasonably compatible' experts but provides no diagnostics for incompatibility detection or analysis of graceful degradation

Ad-hoc technical approximations lacking rigorous justification: conditional sampling (Eq. 7) supported only by intuition and one visual example; velocity summation across experts unexplained; no error analysis provided
Missing critical theoretical analysis: no convergence guarantees, approximation error bounds, or guidance on hyperparameter selection (particle count, MCMC steps, learning rate w)

Evaluation metric concerns: high variance in some metrics (ImageReward ±0.666), heavy reliance on automatic VLM-based evaluation, some improvements within experimental noise (Table 2: LPIPS 0.136 vs 0.164)
Limited technical novelty: AIS and SMC are well-established; main contribution is application to visual generation, which feels incremental
Underdeveloped autoregressive instantiation: Section 3.3 claims support but Appendix C shows limited results; unclear generalization beyond flow models
Missing reproducibility elements: no code availability mentioned, some design choices appear ad-hoc, insufficient ablation studies on particles/MCMC steps/schedules

strengths: Principled probabilistic framework for composing heterogeneous expert models via Product of Experts formulation, with clear mathematical motivation
Novel and comprehensive application of AIS/SMC to compose diverse visual generation sources (generative models, VLMs, physics simulators, graphics engines) in a training-free manner
Demonstrates framework flexibility across four distinct tasks (graphics-engine image editing, physics-guided video, text-to-image with regional composition, and more)
Conditional sampling strategy (Eq. 7) is a practical innovation for reducing multi-modality in expert composition
Well-written overall with clear progression from theory to implementation to experiments
weaknesses: Computational cost is prohibitively high (4-5 min per image, 30 min for text-to-image) severely limiting practical applicability and experimental feasibility. No analysis of computational-quality tradeoffs or faster variants

Experimental scale is very limited: only 30 scenes for image editing, 12 for video generation, and no systematic quantitative evaluation for text-to-image. Insufficient to support strong generalization claims

Evaluation relies exclusively on automatic metrics (GPT-4o, ImageReward, VBench) with no human evaluation studies, limiting confidence in results. LPIPS as foreground metric questionable for comparing natural images to graphics renders

Weak or unfairly-compared baselines: RF-Solver receives different input format (text vs. graphics engine); video baselines (Image2V, Depth2V) not designed for composition; text-to-image lacks comparison with other compositional methods

Technical approximation in Eq. (7) for conditional sampling relies on strong assumptions (conditional independence, Gaussian flow deviations) with only brief justification in appendix. Hyperparameter w not discussed; only basic ablation provided
Limited analysis of failure modes, expert incompatibility, and method robustness. No systematic study of when composition succeeds/fails or guidelines for expert selection
Reproducibility concerns: incomplete project page URL, no code release, scattered implementation details, unjustified hyperparameter choices (T, L, K) with no sensitivity analysis
Missing theoretical analysis: no convergence guarantees, sample complexity bounds, or principled hyperparameter selection. Approximation error in Eq. (7) not quantified
Unclear novelty boundaries: PoE, AIS, and SMC are established techniques; contribution is primarily their engineering application to visual generation rather than algorithmic innovation

Some experimental design issues: arbitrary particle counts and annealing lengths, single-step MCMC per iteration, limited ablations. Results may not demonstrate significant advantages over simpler alternatives

strengths: Principled and comprehensive framework for composing heterogeneous generative and discriminative models at inference time using product distributions
Novel integration of AIS and SMC sampling with conditional generative experts to handle multiple expert types (flow models, autoregressive models, VLMs, physics simulators)
Diverse applications demonstrating practical utility: graphics-engine image editing, physics-simulator video generation, and layout-controlled text-to-image synthesis
Solid technical contributions including clever conditional sampling strategy (Eq. 6) to reduce multi-modality and efficient per-timestep MCMC kernels avoiding weight degeneracy
Comprehensive evaluation with diverse metrics (controllability, quality, alignment) and ablation studies on key components
Clear presentation of methodology with well-documented algorithm and good visualization of the sampling process
weaknesses: Prohibitive computational cost (4 minutes for images, 30 minutes for autoregressive videos) severely limits practical utility with no proposed solutions or efficiency-quality tradeoff analysis

Limited theoretical rigor: no convergence guarantees, approximation error analysis, or justification for key approximations (Eq. 6 conditional sampling, endpoint prediction for discriminative experts)
Small-scale experimental evaluation (30 scenes for graphics, 12-50 scenes for video/text tasks) insufficient for definitive conclusions, with large standard deviations in metrics

Insufficient validation methodology: heavy reliance on automatic metrics (GPT-4o scoring), no human evaluation studies despite claiming improved 'controllability' (subjective property), no inter-rater reliability
Critical assumption of compatible expert predictions acknowledged but inadequately addressed: no method to verify/ensure compatibility, diagnose failures, or guide expert selection
Questionable technical approximations: conditional sampling assumes strong independence (Eq. 9) without justification; endpoint prediction during intermediate steps lacks theoretical analysis
Missing reproducibility details: no mention of code release, unclear hyperparameter selection (T varies from 28-30 without justification), limited sensitivity analysis
Limited comparison scope: only one monolithic baseline in 4.1, no comparison with other recent compositional approaches; simple baselines in 4.2
No systematic analysis of failure modes, incompatible expert combinations, or guidance on when simpler approaches suffice

strengths: Principled probabilistic framework unifying composition of heterogeneous generative and discriminative models, including physics simulators—a meaningful conceptual contribution
Solid technical approach: per-timestep MCMC kernels avoiding weight degeneracy, well-designed integration of AIS and SMC, clear instantiation for both flow and autoregressive models
Comprehensive experimental validation across three diverse and realistic applications (image editing, video generation, text-to-image with layout) with consistent improvements
Multiple well-chosen evaluation metrics (controllability, quality, semantic alignment) with meaningful ablations showing importance of conditional sampling and SMC resampling
Practical flexibility supporting multiple input modalities (text, images, poses, trajectories) with strong qualitative results demonstrating improved controllability and fidelity
Clear technical exposition with well-presented Algorithm 1 and intuitive conditional sampling formulation validated empirically
weaknesses: Significant computational cost (4-30 minutes per sample) acknowledged but unaddressed, limiting practical adoption—unclear if optimization is feasible
Limited scalability: only 2-3 experts evaluated, small experimental datasets (30-50 scenes), paper explicitly defers large-scale sampling to future work, no systematic scalability analysis
Lack of human evaluation studies despite claims of improved 'controllability' and 'user experience'—relies on automatic metrics (VLM-based, LPIPS) which may not correlate with preferences
Expert compatibility assumption underexplored: paper acknowledges incompatible experts require different approaches but provides no guidance, analysis, or robustness evaluation
Conditional sampling approximation (Eq. 9) relies on strong independence assumptions and ad-hoc Gaussian approximation without full justification; no ablation isolating its impact
Limited baseline comparisons—primarily compares against single-expert baselines rather than other composition methods; missing comparisons with recent inference-time guidance approaches
Hyperparameter selection (T, L, K, w) appears task-dependent with limited guidance; sensitivity analysis missing except for particle count in Table 3
Critical technical details (endpoint prediction Eq. 8, conditional sampling justification Section C.3) relegated to appendix rather than main text
